acceptance_rationale: The opening now follows the supervisor argument: real adapters and compactness motivate higher frequency, which introduces switching heat, then zero-voltage-switching and regulation requirements.

The chosen charge-pump and isolated supply is explained before implementation. The user-supplied digest electrical schematic is used directly on s04; native crops carry the charge-transfer and resonant-commutation explanations on s05–s06. The author contribution remains prominent.

Actual V1 burst and carrier captures precede connector regulation and efficiency. The original APEC harmonic-current panel then compares the approximately 80 W USB-C point with IEC Class A individual-current limits; PF and logged THD are retained as summary readings. The notes keep the comparison local to this operating point.

The actual V1 thermal image leads into the distinct original-V2 hot-inductor observation and tank change. V2 power transfer is explained as the expected burst-enable throttle response, with power shown before voltage and all measured points retained. Regional secondary and bridge heating motivates winding, rectifier and current/heat-path improvements.

The conclusion returns to the author integration and secondary-voltage control, 79.89 W connector output and remaining continuous-power limit, without the rejected operating checklist or generic future-measurement slide.

Displayed equations now use editable native Office Math with correct bars, fractions, radicals and variable/subscript typography. Inline circuit variables and backup-table variables use consistent native formatting; mathematical meaning and measured values are unchanged.
